description: KIRA is an independent project focused on creating innovative, accessible applications using NASA's open data, artificial intelligence, and modern web technologies.
summary: KIRA Earth helps people investigate what is changing in Earth's climate, where it is changing, how much, and whether the evidence is statistically significant. Its interactive globe lets users select a place, rank eight NASA POWER climate variables, explore trends through charts, seasonal fingerprints and climate spirals, and cross-check model records against NASA MODIS satellite measurements. Regional maps and a two-region calculator reveal how neighboring or distant places differ, while before-and-after satellite imagery makes environmental change visible. Each result keeps its source, measurement period and uncertainty accessible. Built for students, planners and curious explorers, KIRA Earth turns complex Earth science records into an understandable, repeatable investigation rather than a single unexplained climate headline.
details:
KIRA EARTH — EARTH SYSTEM TREND DETECTIVE

THE PROBLEM

Earth's connected systems change in different directions across regions. A long list of variables and a visually striking map are not enough: people need to know what changed, where, by how much, and how strong the evidence is.

WHAT WE BUILT

KIRA Earth is an interactive globe and 2D map that turns NASA records into a repeatable investigation. Search by place name or coordinates, select a location, then request its evidence. Change Studio ranks eight NASA POWER variables: mean, maximum and minimum air temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind speed, surface pressure and root-zone soil wetness. It also includes an SPI drought index. Seasonal fingerprints, charts, climate spirals and stripes reveal how the record changes through time.

The spatial trend map tests native grid cells within a selected extent. A regional calculator compares two sampled regions, reports trends and uncertainty, and tests whether adding a lagged source-region signal improves predictions over a target-only baseline. It withholds response estimates when validation fails. This is statistical association, not proof that one region causes climatic impacts in another.

Independent satellite evidence includes MODIS vegetation, day/night land-surface temperature, evapotranspiration and productivity records accessed through Microsoft Planetary Computer. Quality flags, coverage and limitations accompany the analysis. Air temperature and satellite surface temperature are different measurements and are identified separately. Before-and-after imagery swipes show visible change, including the Aral Sea; land-cover and surface-water layers add context.

THE SCIENCE AND TRUST

We use Theil–Sen slopes, Mann–Kendall tests, record-length and lag-1 autocorrelation screens, and Benjamini–Hochberg false-discovery-rate control across variable, seasonal or spatial test families. Slopes are reported in native units per decade with intervals and standardized change. A permutation visualization is marked inapplicable when its independence assumptions fail. Missing or unavailable provider values are not replaced with invented data. Sources, dates, units, coverage and uncertainty remain accessible.

A current-weather panel adds WeatherNext 2 and ECMWF ensemble context through Open-Meteo. Weather forecasts are distinct from observed long-term trends and are not climate projections. Optional local analog intelligence uses Laya to compare historical patterns; the lightweight public deployment excludes neural checkpoints and uses the documented fallback. It does not claim to run Laya in the cloud.

IMPACT AND CREATIVITY

Students, journalists, planners and curious explorers can move from a location to an understandable evidence trail. Our distinctive combination is automatic variable screening, comparable standardized trends, seasonal animation, significance screening, satellite cross-checks and two-region comparison in one progressive interface. A guided tour follows a concrete Cairo investigation rather than leaving users with an unexplained map.

IMPLEMENTATION AND VALIDATION

React, TypeScript, CesiumJS, Recharts and Vite power the interface. Python FastAPI, NumPy, pandas, SciPy, xarray and ecCodes support the backend. A Docker container serves the frontend and API on Render Free. The production build and 126 automated tests passed. We verified Cairo Studio, the WeatherNext 2 forecast and Cairo–Nairobi Compare on the public deployment; the team also confirmed the globe and Cairo load on a phone. Free hosting can cold-start, and regional values are weighted grid samples rather than full-area or station averages. Scientific limitations and open improvements are documented in the repository.

AI / SI DISCLOSURE

Code, documentation and presentation were developed with assistance from Anthropic Claude Code and OpenAI Codex. Scientific statistics are calculated from provider records, not generated as fictional measurements. The 30-second demo edits a recording of the real application; its captions and end card use HyperFrames. The narration is AI-generated locally with Kokoro-82M (af_heart), not a cloned voice. That disclosure appears on screen, is spoken in the outro, and is included in metadata. Optional in-app generated explanations are labelled. NASA is identified as a data source; no NASA branding was generated for this project. Full details: https://github.com/saggamer/kira-earth/blob/main/AI_USE.md

PUBLIC LINKS

Source code and methods: https://github.com/saggamer/kira-earth

NASA GMAO MERRA-2 — source reanalysis for POWER meteorology
NASA GIBS — MODIS and GPM imagery service
MODIS Terra MOD11A2 v061 — 8-day land-surface temperature
MODIS Terra MOD13A1 v061 — vegetation indices / NDVI
MODIS Terra MOD16A3GF v061 — annual evapotranspiration
MODIS Terra MOD17A3HGF v061 — annual net primary productivity
NASA FIRMS — optional VIIRS active-fire detections
NASA Blue Marble — offline basemap fallback
projectRefs: Microsoft Planetary Computer — STAC and MODIS access
Impact Observatory / Microsoft / Esri — 10 m annual land cover
European Commission JRC — Global Surface Water
ECMWF open data — AIFS atmospheric fields and IFS ensemble
Google DeepMind WeatherNext 2 — AI ensemble via Open-Meteo
Open-Meteo — forecast, ensemble and geocoding APIs
Copernicus CAMS — air-quality data via Open-Meteo
US National Weather Service — public alerts API
Laya — optional local climate-pattern resemblance model
Anthropic Claude API — optional generated explanations
OpenAI Codex — AI-assisted coding, review and documentation
Kokoro-82M — AI-generated demo narration, voice af_heart
Kokoro ONNX — local narration synthesis runtime
HyperFrames — editable demo composition, captions and rendering
FFmpeg — demo video and audio processing
Google Fonts — Inter, Space Grotesk and JetBrains Mono
